title: Letter Grade from a Score
oneLiner: Turn a score from 0 to 100 into a letter with an else-if chain, and reject scores outside the range.
keyTakeaway: Check invalid input first, then test thresholds from highest to lowest so each branch only needs one comparison. Boundary values (exactly 90, exactly 0, exactly 100) are where else-if chains go wrong, so test them.
explanation:
Return the letter grade for a whole-number score: 90 to 100 is "A", 80 to 89 "B", 70 to 79 "C", 60 to 69 "D", and 0 to 59 "F". A score below 0 or above 100 isn't valid: return "Invalid".

Deal with the invalid case first, then go from the top down: if the score is at least 90 it's an A; otherwise, if it's at least 80, it's a B; and so on. Because each else-if only runs when every earlier test failed, you never need to write both ends of a range (score >= 80 && score < 90). The order is what makes that safe: test 60 before 90 and every passing score becomes a D.

In C#, a switch expression with relational patterns reads nicely too: score switch { < 0 or > 100 => "Invalid", >= 90 => "A", ... }. In Python, an if/elif chain is the clearest.

visualizationSteps.message: Grade a score of 72. The checks run left to right and stop at the first that matches.
72 is between 0 and 100, so it's valid. Carry on.
72 >= 70? Yes: the grade is "C". The remaining checks never run.

complexity.note: At most six comparisons, however large the score.
